claimChecks.claim: Lipari has ancient places now below the sea.
claimChecks.basis: P1 says terrestrial and underwater archaeological sites; P3 says progressive submersion of coastal archaeological/historical sites.

claimChecks.claim: Study reconstructs coastal changes over 3,900 years.
claimChecks.basis: Article title gives 3,900 years; P4 says last four millennia and specifically last 3,900 years. We retain precision without annual-rate forecast.

claimChecks.claim: Researchers from multiple institutions/universities including INGV cooperated.
claimChecks.basis: Named international research team includes INGV, CNR, universities and archaeological collaborators.

claimChecks.claim: Bronze Age archaeological traces at Pignataro di Fuori lie 20–42 m deep.
claimChecks.basis: Exact range and site in unquoted narrative. Wording says located there, not newly discovered by this study.
Archaeological markers support reconstruction; site testifies to coastal landscape evolution.

claimChecks.claim: Land subsided and sea level rose over time.
claimChecks.basis: P1 explicitly describes increased sea level over time; P4 estimates island lowering. No rate or future precision added.

claimChecks.claim: These changes contributed to submergence of coastal ancient sites.
claimChecks.basis: Narrative links geological/tectonic/volcanic processes and sea-level increase with submergence. Contribuito preserves a contributory, not exhaustive explanation.

claimChecks.claim: Site opens opportunities to locate/study other ancient settlements.
claimChecks.basis: Exact research prospect; pedagogical gloss explains insediamenti as places people lived.

claimChecks.claim: Work may help find additional Bronze Age sites along Mediterranean coasts.
claimChecks.basis: Article says new research prospects, including other Mediterranean coasts. Conditional potrebbe prevents treating prospects as discoveries.
